correctness.rationale: The generator on the disagreement-count state k has rates k to k-1 and ck/n to n-k. Dividing its exact finite backward equations by k and summing gives τ_n=nH_n/(n+c); its k=n boundary gives τ_{n-1}=H_{n-1}, and k=1 gives τ_1=(n+cH_{n-1})/(n+c). All states are transient except 0 and mean absorption finite for c>0. The martingale with weights degree/flip rate gives the two exact fixation probabilities. Difference numerators are affine in c with unique roots. The independently implemented full binary-state generator and lumped generator agree exactly for 28 and 77 rational examples respectively; infinite quantifiers are established by the proof, not code.

originality.rationale: The four highly relevant primary texts were compared at the level of their rate generators, graph class, initial conditions, and exact versus asymptotic conclusions. Sood–Antal–Redner (2007/2008) cover uniform-rate degree heterogeneity, Masuda–Gibert–Redner (2010) intrinsic rates mainly on regular graphs, Hadjichrysanthou–Broom–Rychtař (2011) type-dependent fitness on stars, and Iwamasa–Masuda (2014) unit-rate graph-topology comparisons. value.rationale: Intrinsic response-rate heterogeneity is a substantive social-dynamics variable. The all-n comparison reveals a nonempty interval in which hub-seeded opinion is more likely to win yet yields faster unconditional consensus than leaf-seeded opinion. The two thresholds are explicit and separated by (n-1)/H_{n-1}~n/log n, and the penultimate discordance state's mean duration is invariant under arbitrarily changing center rate. This is a complete structural rate-size classification, beyond a routine one-parameter numeric sweep.
